title: [recoverability] The store of secrets by name and `spawn secret set|generate|list` (design-secret-injection step B): a value only from a pipe or a terminal without echo, never an argument, a file or /dev/null; no command prints a value (no get); tier 2 refused (nothing injectable); a crash stores nothing
prompt:
Spawn, mission 4, objective 122 [recoverability]: the store of secrets by name, and its admin command `spawn secret set|generate|list`. This is build step B of sync/design-secret-injection.md (sha ae1f0149), section 5, under section 0's owner decisions of 2026-11-13: agents keep root, nothing is injectable (tier 2 ships empty), and the store's backup is sealed to a key pair whose private half is on the Mac only. The approved split: 122 is the store with set, generate and list; 123 (rotate, retired values, the keyed fingerprint) and 124 (the sealed backup) come after it lands. Size above the guide: the lock and leftover recovery (rev-e F1) belong with set; split rejected by the lead.

Why. Every leak in the record came from a secret in a file, an environment, a command line or a printed connection string that the agents' own user reads in ordinary work. A store whose admin command never takes a value as an argument, never prints one and has no `get` closes those accidental paths for every secret moved into it. Root can still read the store (section 0, decision 1); this objective does not try to stop that.

Required behaviour.
- The store is the directory SPAWN_SECRET_STORE names: an absolute path to an existing directory, owned by the running user, mode 700, and not a symbolic link (checked without following it). Otherwise every command refuses and writes nothing. Who owns the installed store (root or spawn-secrets) is the install step's choice, not this objective's: nothing here installs anything.
- Layout: <store>/<NAME> holds the value exactly (mode 600). <store>/<NAME>.json (mode 600) holds {"name", "tier": 1, "created": RFC 3339}, never the value. Each file is written to a new staged file (create-new, 600), fsynced, then hard-linked to its name (never over an existing name); the staged file is removed and the directory fsynced. A crash leaves no partial value under a name.
- A write (set, generate) holds the store's lock (an exclusive lock on the store directory) from its last check to its fsync, taken after the value is read; list takes the shared lock. Under the write lock no other write is in progress, so what a killed write left is known to be a leftover:
  - every staged file (`.<file>.<pid>.new`) is removed;
  - an incomplete entry of the name being written (its value without its metadata, or its metadata without its value) is replaced, and the success line says so. The killed write never printed "stored".
  - list names each leftover, never with a value: `NAME  incomplete: …` and `.<file>.<pid>.new  staged: …`.
- A name is [A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}. Anything else is refused and creates nothing. An existing name (its value and its metadata both present) is refused, and its value stays; a new value is 123's rotation.
- `spawn secret set NAME [--tier 1]` reads the value from stdin, and only:
  - from a pipe (stdin is a FIFO); or
  - from a terminal: with echo off and keyboard signals off (stty -echo -icanon -isig), read byte by byte, with a prompt on stderr. Enter (or Ctrl-D) ends the value; backspace erases one character (a whole UTF-8 sequence); Ctrl-U erases the line; Ctrl-C cancels with exit 2 and nothing stored. The saved settings (stty -g) are restored on every path, including when setting the new ones fails. Because the keys are read as bytes, a keyboard signal (Ctrl-C, Ctrl-\, Ctrl-Z) cannot leave echo off; a SIGTERM or SIGKILL at the prompt can, and nothing is stored or printed then. The terminal takes any bytes, as the pipe does.
  stdin that is neither (/dev/null, a regular file, a socket) is refused with a sentence that says the value comes from a pipe or a terminal. One trailing "\n" or "\r\n" is not part of the value. An empty value is refused and nothing is stored. A value over 64 KiB is refused.
- Any extra word after `set NAME` (it may be the value) is refused with a sentence that never repeats it. `--tier 2` is refused, before any value is read, as "no secret is injectable" (owner decision 2). Any other tier is refused.
- `spawn secret generate NAME --bytes N` makes N random bytes (16..=1024, from /dev/urandom) inside the store, as base64url without padding. Nothing prints them. N outside the range is refused.
- `spawn secret list` prints one line per secret, sorted: `NAME  tier=1  created=<time>`. It never prints a value. An empty store prints nothing, exit 0.
- `get`, and every other verb, prints the usage, which says there is no get, and exits 2. No command prints a value, anywhere.
- Every refusal is one sentence on stderr beginning "spawn secret: ", with exit 2. Success prints one line naming the secret, never its value, with exit 0.
- The words the acceptance reads (the rest of each sentence is free):
  - unset store: "SPAWN_SECRET_STORE is not set";
  - any other refused store: "must be an existing directory of yours, mode 700";
  - an empty value: "empty";
  - tier 2: "injectable";
  - the usage: begins "usage: spawn secret";
  - the terminal prompt: holds "not echoed";
  - list's leftover rows: "<NAME>  incomplete" and "<file>  staged" at the line's start;
  - the metadata's "created" is a string beginning with a four-digit year.
- `spawn` with no arguments lists `spawn secret set|generate|list` in its usage.

Files (expected; no other open objective touches them): crates/spawn-cli/src/secret.rs (new) and crates/spawn-cli/src/main.rs (`mod secret;`, the dispatch line and one usage line). One crate. Size: the throwaway is +483/-1, of which 72 lines are unit tests and about 60 doc comments.

Unit tests: base64url (no padding, the URL alphabet, 32 bytes give 43 characters); names (good ones, and "", lower case, a leading digit or underscore, "-", "../A", "A/B", "A.json", 65 characters refused); set's flags (an extra word refused without repeating it, tier 2 refused as not injectable, tier 1 and nothing accepted); the terminal line (Enter, CR, Ctrl-D and end of input end it; backspace erases a whole character; Ctrl-U erases the line; Ctrl-C cancels without repeating what was typed); staged names (dotted .new files only, not .fingerprint.key).

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/122.sh. Black box, with made-up values (random per run) under a scratch root and a scratch HOME. Nothing outside the scratch root is read or written.
(1) A store that is unset, relative, missing, mode 755 or a symlink to a 700 directory is refused (exit 2) by every command, and nothing is written.
(2) list on an empty store prints nothing, exit 0.
(3) set from a pipe stores the value exactly at mode 600, with one trailing "\n" or "\r\n" dropped whole, and with metadata that holds no value.
(4) A value given as an argument is refused and never repeated.
(5) stdin that is /dev/null or a regular file is refused; an empty value is refused; nothing is stored.
(6) An existing name is refused and keeps its value.
(7) --tier 2 is refused as not injectable, before any value is read.
(8) generate makes N random bytes as base64url, different each time; --bytes outside 16..1024 is refused.
(9) list names every secret with tier=1 and created=, and no value. The store holds each secret's two files and nothing else: no staged copy is left behind.
(10) get, dump, show and export are refused with the usage, exit 2, and print no value.
(11) A name that is not [A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63} is refused and creates nothing.
(12) From a terminal (a pty), the typed value is stored exactly and never echoed; a character typed and erased is not part of it. Ctrl-C at the prompt stores nothing, exits 2, and leaves the terminal's echo on (stty -a in the same pty after set).
(13) While set reads from a slow pipe, no process's argv holds the value or its first part.
(14) set killed (SIGKILL) in the middle of reading stores nothing, list does not name it, and the part read is in no file under the scratch root.
(15) No value is in any command's output or in any file outside the store, and nothing is written in HOME.
(16) A killed write's leftovers, planted by hand (a value without its metadata, metadata without its value, a staged copy): list names each and exits 0; the next set of another name removes the staged copy; set and generate of the incomplete names replace them, and list then shows them as stored.

Verified by: after it lands and is deployed, the lead runs the deployed `spawn secret` against a scratch store (mktemp -d, chmod 700) with made-up values only: set from a pipe, set at a terminal (the value not echoed), generate, list, and get refused. No live path, no unit and no sudoers are touched. Installing the store root-owned is a later step with its own review.
